passages.t: ‘Like a weaned child with his mother’
passages.happening:
Psalm 131 is only three verses long. The heading reads, “A song of ascents. Of David” (verse 1). The prayer begins with what the singer is not. “My heart is not proud, O LORD, my eyes are not haughty. I do not aspire to great things or matters too lofty for me” (verse 1).

Then what he has done. “Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul; like a weaned child with his mother, like a weaned child is my soul within me” (verse 2).

Last, he turns to everyone. “O Israel, put your hope in the LORD, both now and forevermore” (verse 3).
passages.hearers:
A lifted heart and raised eyes were Hebrew ways of describing pride, someone who looks down on others or reaches above his place. The singer says he has put that down. He has stopped grasping at things too big for him.

The picture in verse 2 is the heart of the psalm. In ancient Israel children were often nursed much longer than many are today. Hannah waited until Samuel was weaned before she brought him to the house of the LORD (1 Samuel 1:24). Abraham held a feast the day Isaac was weaned (Genesis 21:8). A nursing baby cries and reaches whenever it is hungry. A weaned child can sit with its mother without demanding anything. It is simply content to be near her.

That is the soul in this psalm: no longer restless and grabbing, but quiet in God's presence. Notice the words ‘I have stilled and quieted’. It took effort. Calm did not just arrive.

The image is a mother's lap, and the psalm does not hesitate to use it of God's care. The note on Psalm 120 explains the Songs of Ascents.
passages.later:
Jesus said, “unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 18:3). He also said, “learn from Me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls” (Matthew 11:29).

Paul wrote, “I have learned to be content regardless of my circumstances” (Philippians 4:11). He too had to learn it.
passages.asks:
Is your soul like a nursing baby, crying for what it wants right now? Or like a weaned child, at rest because it trusts the one it is with?

Psalm 131 asks you to set down some of the questions too big for you, and some of the ambitions you have been grabbing at. It does not say they do not matter. It says you can be quiet with God while they wait.
